title: PQ-zkSDK Security Descriptor
description: Machine-readable cryptographic provenance record for a zkSDK primitive. Consumed by @zksdk/pq-audit, compliance reports, and GRC integrations. Hybrid primitives declare BOTH halves machine-readably: the classical half in classical_component, the PQ half in pq_component. The audit tool reads classical exposure from classical_component — never from prose notes.

mode.description: Active cryptographic mode. Hybrid is the default for kit primitives.

assumption_family.description: Underlying hardness assumption of the primitive as a whole. 'hybrid' means a combination that survives if one family breaks. A descriptor whose overall family is 'pairing' or 'dlog' is Shor-broken and must declare quantum_security_bits: 0.

classical_component.description: The classical half of the primitive. All fields 'none' in pq-only mode. Machine-readable so the audit tool can inventory classical (Shor-exposed) surface without parsing notes.

pq_component.description: The post-quantum (or Grover-only, hash-based) half of the primitive. All fields 'none' in classical mode. FN-DSA (Falcon) is intentionally absent until FIPS 206 is finalized.

wrapper.description: NOTE: a groth16_bn254 wrapper around a PQ proof makes on-chain soundness classical-only — the descriptor must not claim PQ soundness for the wrapped verification path.

classical_security_bits.description: Estimated cost of the best classical attack, in bits. Name the metric and the component it comes from in notes (e.g. 'floor of the two components').

quantum_security_bits.description: Estimated post-quantum security in bits. MUST be 0 for anything whose overall assumption family is Shor-broken (ECDLP, DLP, pairings). For hash-based schemes, reflect the Grover-reduced margin. A nonzero value requires a genuine PQ or hash basis (enforced below). Name the metric in notes.

onchain_soundness.description: What the on-chain verification path actually enforces. 'classical_only' when only the classical proof (e.g. Groth16) is verified on-chain — regardless of what is verified off-chain. 'hybrid_pq' requires a PQ-sound proof actually verified on-chain. Commitments to off-chain verification results do NOT count as hybrid_pq.

fips_conformance.description: Algorithm-level conformance to the named FIPS, verified via NIST test vectors in CI. Use ['none'] if not verified — regardless of which library is used. IMPORTANT: this asserts algorithm conformance ONLY. It does NOT assert FIPS 140-3 / CMVP module validation; no package in this kit is a validated cryptographic module, and entities with validated-module obligations cannot discharge them with this kit. Generated reports must carry this disclaimer.

nist_security_category.description: NIST security category (1-5) of the PQ component's parameter set, per FIPS 203/204/205. NIST assigns categories, not single bit numbers — report the category alongside any conservative bit estimate, and name the metric behind the bits in notes.

cavp_validation.description: CAVP algorithm certificate ID if the implementation holds one; 'none' otherwise. Distinct from passing KATs in CI (fips_conformance) and from CMVP module validation.

cmvp_validation.description: FIPS 140-3 CMVP module certificate ID; 'none' otherwise. No kit package is a validated module.

status.description: Maturity. Anything without a third-party audit is 'experimental' at most, never 'production'.

last_reviewed.description: When these claims were last checked against current cryptanalysis. A stale date is itself a signal.

notes.description: Caveats — especially anything that downgrades confidence in the numeric claims, and the metric behind each *_security_bits value.

allOf.$comment: 'none' in fips_conformance is exclusive — it cannot appear alongside a real conformance claim.
A fips_203 claim requires an ML-KEM in the PQ component.
A fips_204 claim requires an ML-DSA in the PQ component.
A fips_205 claim requires an SLH-DSA in the PQ component.
Classical mode carries no active PQ component.
pq-only mode carries no active classical component.
Hybrid mode requires a real algorithm on BOTH sides — a 'hybrid' of one component is a mislabel.
A Groth16 L1 verifier enforces classical soundness only — the descriptor must say so.
Shor-broken assumption families must declare zero quantum security, in every mode.

A nonzero quantum claim requires a genuine basis: a hash assumption family, or an active PQ component. (This replaces the old rule that MANDATED quantum_security_bits >= 1 from mode alone, which could force a false claim.)
An active classical component with NO PQ component is dlog/pairing cryptography and must say so (which in turn forces quantum_security_bits: 0 above).
A groth16_bn254 wrapper makes on-chain soundness classical-only: the wrapped verification rests on BN254 pairing (Shor-broken). It must NOT claim onchain_soundness: hybrid_pq.

onchain_soundness: hybrid_pq requires a PQ-sound proof ACTUALLY verified on-chain — an active PQ (STARK) proof system AND an on-chain verifier that checks it (a STARK verifier). offchain_only, a Groth16 verifier, or 'none' can never be hybrid_pq; a commitment to an off-chain result does not count.
ML-KEM-512 is NIST Category 1: cap declared category at 1 and quantum_security_bits at a conservative 128 (AES-128-comparable). Prevents category/bit overclaims on a real PQ primitive.
ML-KEM-768 is NIST Category 3: cap category at 3 and quantum_security_bits at a conservative 192 (AES-192-comparable).
ML-KEM-1024 is NIST Category 5: cap category at 5 and quantum_security_bits at a conservative 256 (AES-256-comparable).
ML-DSA-44 is NIST Category 2: cap category at 2 and quantum_security_bits at a conservative 128 (tracks the ~128-bit target of the rest of the stack; THREAT-MODEL §4.1).
ML-DSA-65 is NIST Category 3: cap category at 3 and quantum_security_bits at a conservative 192.
ML-DSA-87 is NIST Category 5: cap category at 5 and quantum_security_bits at a conservative 256.

SLH-DSA-128 (SHA2 or SHAKE, s or f) is NIST Category 1: cap category at 1 and quantum_security_bits at a conservative 128. (Hash-based: the Grover-reduced margin lives here, and the parameter sets are the 128-bit family.)

activeComponent.$comment: At least one of kem / signature / proof_system is not 'none'.
